\section{Turing Machine --- Universal Block}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.UniversalBlock
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Universal Block: Introduction}

This module completes the live serialized-table block of the universal Turing
machine (Arora--Barak, \S 1.4.1, Theorem~1.9): exact-cost skipping and
selection of transition records over the canonical serialized table, reading
of the eight fixed action bits, successor decoding and installation, and the
application of the decoded record, assembled into the block lemma that one
live step of the simulated machine is realized by the fixed four-tape table
interpreter within a code-dependent budget.  It also provides the concrete
checkpoint relation between source and universal-machine configurations,
its startup, halting, and output correspondence lemmas, and the block budget
itself.  Throughout, bit strings are written over $\{0,1\}$ ($1$ for true,
$0$ for false), $1^n$ denotes $n$ consecutive $1$s, and ``the table is
$w$'' means that the interpreter's first work tape is the two-way infinite
tape holding the bit string $w$ in cells $0, \dots, |w| - 1$ with blanks
elsewhere, its cursor position counted from cell $0$.

\subsection*{Turing Machine --- Universal Block: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Exact-Cost Skip of a Unary Field]
\lean{Turing.universal_skip_unary}
\label{Turing.universal_skip_unary}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.universalEvalCfg, Turing.universalEval_step, Turing.universalFour, Turing.universalInterpreter, Turing.universalSkipDone}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a Boolean input string, $b$ a four-tape interpreter configuration on $x$, $d$
a destination control index or no destination, $r$ a remaining-record count from $0$
through $8$, and $T$ a table decomposed as $T=l1^n0r'$. Starting in the unary-skipping
phase with registers $d,r$, table cursor $|l|$, state tape $\sigma$, and state cursor
$s$, after $n+1$ interpreter steps the cursor is $|l|+n+1$ and the control is the
continuation for $d$ if $r=0$, or the fixed-field skipping phase with count $r-1$ and
field index $0$ otherwise; the state tape and cursor are unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exact-Cost Skip of One Record]
\lean{Turing.universal_skip_record}
\label{Turing.universal_skip_record}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.universalActionBits, Turing.universalEvalCfg, Turing.universalInterpreter, Turing.universalNextOnes, Turing.universalRecordBits, Turing.universalSkipDone, Turing.universal_record_shape, Turing.universal_skip_fixed, Turing.universal_skip_unary}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a Boolean input string, $b$ a four-tape interpreter configuration on $x$, $d$
a destination control index or no destination, $r$ a remaining-record count from $0$
through $8$, and $T$ a table decomposed as $T=l\rho r'$, where $\rho$ is the serialized
record of an action of a one-work-tape binary machine. From the fixed-field skipping
phase with registers $d,r$, field index $0$, table cursor $|l|$, state tape $\sigma$,
and state cursor $s$, after $|\rho|$ interpreter steps the table cursor is $|l|+|\rho|$
and the control is the continuation for $d$ if $r=0$, or the fixed-field skipping phase
with remaining count $r-1$ and field index $0$ otherwise; the state tape and state
cursor are unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Skipping Consecutive Record Groups]
\lean{Turing.universal_skip_groups}
\label{Turing.universal_skip_groups}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.universalEvalCfg, Turing.universalEval_step, Turing.universalFour, Turing.universalInterpreter, Turing.universalRecordBits, Turing.universalSkipDone, Turing.universalStateWindow, Turing.universalStateWindow_end, Turing.universalStateWindow_erase, Turing.universalStateWindow_read, Turing.universal_skip_records}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$ be a Boolean input string, $b$ a four-tape interpreter configuration on $x$, $i$
a record index from $0$ through $8$, and $T$ a table decomposed as $T=lGr$, where $G$ is
the concatenation of the serialized records in a list of groups, each group containing
exactly nine actions. For any natural number $n$, let the state tape have a marker at
position $0$ and unary cells in the window from $j+1$ through $j+g$, where $j$ is the
number of already consumed unary cells and $g$ is the number of groups; then, after
$g+|G|+1$ interpreter steps from the record-group phase at table cursor $|l|$ and state
cursor $j+1$, the interpreter is in the state-rewind phase remembering $i$, with table
cursor $|l|+|G|$, state tape corresponding to $j+g$ consumed cells and no remaining
unary cells, and state cursor $j+g+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Reading the fixed action fields]
\lean{Turing.universal_read_fixed}
\label{Turing.universal_read_fixed}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.universalEvalCfg, Turing.universalEval_step, Turing.universalFour, Turing.universalInterpreter}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let the base configuration be a four-tape configuration
on input $x$, let $T=l\,b_0b_1\cdots b_7\,r$ for finite bit strings $l,r$ and bits
$b_0,\ldots,b_7$, and let the state tape, its cursor, and an eight-bit register be
specified. For every natural number $n$, field index $f\in\{0,\ldots,7\}$, and register
$old$, if $f+n=7$ and $old$ agrees with the corresponding bit of $T$ at every index
below $f$, then after $n+1$ interpreter steps from the action-reading phase at cursor
$|l|+f$, the interpreter is in the successor-decoding phase with register equal to the
eight bits of $T$ and cursor $|l|+8$, while the state tape, its cursor, and all other
configuration data are unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Cost of successor preparation]
\lean{Turing.universalNextCost}
\label{Turing.universalNextCost}
\leanok
The number of interpreter steps needed to decode the successor field of a
serialized record and install the successor state in unary, before the
decoded action is applied: $1$ when there is no successor state (the action
halts), and $2q + 4$ when the successor state has index $q$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Successor state preparation]
\lean{Turing.universal_prepare_next}
\label{Turing.universal_prepare_next}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.universalEvalCfg, Turing.universalEval_step, Turing.universalFour, Turing.universalInterpreter, Turing.universalNextCost, Turing.universalNextOnes, Turing.universalStateTape, Turing.universalStateTape_marker, Turing.universal_state_rewind, Turing.universal_unary_copy}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let the base configuration be a four-tape configuration
on input $x$, and let $T$ be a table of the form $l\,1^u\,0\,r$, where $u$ is the unary
size of an optional successor state: it is $0$ if there is no successor, and $q+1$ if
the successor has index $q$. For any eight-bit action register and any such optional
successor, starting in the successor-decoding phase with table cursor $|l|$, the unary
tape encoding of state $0$, and state cursor $1$, after exactly $1$ steps if the
successor is absent or $2q+4$ steps if its index is $q$, the interpreter is in the
record-application phase with the same action register, a flag indicating whether the
successor is absent, table cursor $|l|+u$, the unary encoding of state $0$ if absent or
state $q$ otherwise, and state cursor $1$; all other configuration data are inherited
from the base configuration.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[The nine actions of a coded state]
\lean{Turing.universalActions}
\label{Turing.universalActions}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.CodeTM}
For a coded machine $M$ and a state $q$ of $M$, the list of the nine
transition actions of $q$: for each input read and each work read, ranging
over blank, $0$, $1$ in the fixed serialization order with the input read
varying slowest, the action $M$ performs at $q$ on that read pair.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Lookup in a state transition block]
\lean{Turing.universalActions_lookup}
\label{Turing.universalActions_lookup}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeTM, Turing.universalActions, Turing.universalRecordIndex}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a coded one-work-tape machine and let $q$ be one of its states. For any input
read and work-tape read, each either blank, $0$, or $1$, the list of transition actions
for $q$ has length $9$, and its entry at index $3r_{\mathrm{in}}+r_{\mathrm{work}}$ is
the action prescribed by $M$ for those reads, where the blank, $0$, and $1$ have indices
$0$, $1$, and $2$, respectively.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Header of the canonical serialization]
\lean{Turing.universalHeader}
\label{Turing.universalHeader}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeTM, Turing.pairEncode}
The header of the canonical serialization of a coded machine $M$ with state
count $m$ and initial state index $q_0$: the pair encoding of the binary
digit string of $m$ with the empty string (each digit doubled, then the
unequal delimiter pair), followed by $1^{q_0} \cdot 0$, the initial state
in unary with its terminator.  It comprises everything preceding the
transition records.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Serialization by Header and Action Groups]
\lean{Turing.universal_serialization_actions}
\label{Turing.universal_serialization_actions}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeTM, Turing.CodeTM.serialize, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.universalActions, Turing.universalHeader, Turing.universalRecordBits, Turing.universalRecords}
\difficulty{5}
For every machine $M$ in code normal form, its canonical serialization is its header
followed by the concatenation, in increasing state order, of the serialized transition
records of that state's nine actions, ordered with the input read varying slowest and
the work read varying fastest.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Transition table decomposition]
\lean{Turing.universal_lookup_parts}
\label{Turing.universal_lookup_parts}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.CodeTM, Turing.CodeTM.serialize, Turing.universalActions, Turing.universalActions_lookup, Turing.universalHeader, Turing.universalRecordBits, Turing.universalRecordIndex, Turing.universal_serialization_actions}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a machine in code normal form, let $q$ be one of its states, and let $u,w$
each be a blank symbol or a bit. The canonical serialization of $M$ consists of its
header, followed by the serialized records of a list of exactly $q$ groups, each
containing nine actions, followed by the serialized records of a list of actions whose
length is the index of the read pair $(u,w)$, then the record for the action prescribed
by $M$ in state $q$ on reads $(u,w)$, and finally a remaining bit string.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Decoding the eight action bits]
\lean{Turing.universalActionBits_decode}
\label{Turing.universalActionBits_decode}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.universalActionBits, Turing.universalSign, Turing.universalWrite}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$ and every one-work-tape action $a$ over the Boolean
alphabet, the two-bit fields at positions $0,1$ and $4,5$ decode to the input-head and
work-head movements of $a$, respectively, while the field at positions $2,3$ decodes to
its optional work-tape write and the field at positions $6,7$ recovers its optional
output symbol.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Applying a decoded transition record]
\lean{Turing.universal_apply_record}
\label{Turing.universal_apply_record}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.CodeTM, Turing.CodeTM.serialize, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.virtualMove, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.universalActionBits, Turing.universalActionBits_decode, Turing.universalEvalCfg, Turing.universalFour, Turing.universalInput_move, Turing.universalInput_read, Turing.universalInterpreter, Turing.universalSimulationCfg, Turing.universalStateTape}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a coded machine, let $\alpha$ and $x$ be bit strings, let $s$ be a
configuration of $M$ on input $x$, and let $a$ be a one-step action for $M$. For any
natural numbers $\mathit{oldp}$ and $p$, one step of the universal interpreter from the
evaluation configuration based on the simulation checkpoint of $s$ at cursor
$\mathit{oldp}$, in the record-application control state carrying the eight bits of $a$
and the flag indicating whether $a$ halts, with table $M$’s canonical serialization at
cursor $p$ and the successor state’s unary tape (using state index $0$ if $a$ halts) at
cursor $1$, equals the simulation checkpoint of the configuration obtained by applying
$a$ to $s$, at table cursor $p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exact-cost record selection]
\lean{Turing.universal_select}
\label{Turing.universal_select}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action, Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.UniversalControl, Turing.universalEvalCfg, Turing.universalInterpreter, Turing.universalRecordBits, Turing.universalSkipDone, Turing.universalStateTape, Turing.universalStateTape_marker, Turing.universalStateWindow_empty, Turing.universalStateWindow_zero, Turing.universal_skip_groups, Turing.universal_skip_records, Turing.universal_state_rewind}
\difficulty{5}
Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let the base configuration be a four-tape configuration
on input $x$, let $i$ be an index from $0$ through $8$, and let the table be
$l\,G\,B\,r$. Suppose $G$ is the concatenation of the serialized records in a list of
groups, each containing exactly nine one-work-tape binary machine actions; suppose $B$
is the concatenation of the serialized records of a list of actions of length $i$; and
suppose the state tape encodes the number $g$ of groups in unary, with its cursor at
$1$. Starting in the record-group phase with index $i$ and table cursor $|l|$, after
exactly $2g+|G|+|B|+3$ steps the interpreter is in the action-reading phase at field $0$
with its bit register cleared, table cursor $|l|+|G|+|B|$, and state tape encoding $0$
in unary with cursor $1$; the other configuration data are inherited from the base
configuration.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Concatenation of machine runs]
\lean{Turing.universal_run_join}
\label{Turing.universal_run_join}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{1}
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the binary alphabet, and let $a,b,c$ be
configurations on a common input. If running $M$ for $s$ steps from $a$ yields $b$, and
running it for $t$ steps from $b$ yields $c$, then running it for $s+t$ steps from $a$
yields $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[The block budget]
\lean{Turing.universalBlockBound}
\label{Turing.universalBlockBound}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeTM.serialize, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode}
The code-dependent block budget of the universal machine for an effective
machine-coding scheme on a code string $\alpha$:
\[
  3L + 5(N + 1) + 20,
\]
where $L$ is the length of the canonical serialization of the machine
decoded from $\alpha$ and $N$ is that machine's state count.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The concrete checkpoint relation]
\lean{Turing.universalRelation}
\label{Turing.universalRelation}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.CodeTM.serialize, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode, Turing.FinTM.rightCfg, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.universalCanonTM, Turing.universalSimulationCfg, Turing.universalTM}
For an effective machine-coding scheme $c$, a code string $\alpha$, and an
input $x$: the relation between a configuration $s$ of the machine decoded
from $\alpha$ (in one-work-tape form) on $x$ and a configuration $t$ of the
complete universal-machine candidate on the pair encoding
$\langle \alpha, x \rangle$ that holds when there exist a table cursor $p$
not exceeding the length of the canonical serialization of the decoded
machine, together with contents and head positions for the inactive
canonizer tapes, such that $t$ is the right-block embedding, over those
inactive tapes, of the interpreter checkpoint of $s$ with table cursor
$p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Length bound for the serialized header]
\lean{Turing.universal_header_bound}
\label{Turing.universal_header_bound}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeTM, Turing.CodeTM.serialize, Turing.universal_pair_length, Turing.universal_serialization_header}
\difficulty{3}
For every machine $M$ in code normal form, let $m$ be its state-count parameter and
$q_0$ its initial state index. If $\ell$ is the number of bits in the binary
representation of $m$ and $L$ is the length of its canonical serialization, then
$2\ell+2+q_0+1\le L$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Startup reaches the simulation relation]
\lean{Turing.universalRelation_start}
\label{Turing.universalRelation_start}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.EffectiveMachineCode, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.universalRelation, Turing.universalStartupBound, Turing.universalTM, Turing.universal_header_bound, Turing.universal_initialized}
\difficulty{1}
Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme, and let $\alpha$ and $x$ be finite bit
strings. There is a natural number $t$ bounded above by $3|\alpha|$ plus the canonizer's
time bound at $|\alpha|$, the length of the serialization of the machine decoded from
$\alpha$, twice the length of the binary expansion of its number of states, twice its
initial state index, and $12$, such that the universal machine associated with $c$,
started on the paired encoding of $\alpha$ and $x$, reaches after $t$ steps a
configuration related to the decoded machine's initial configuration on input $x$ by the
following relation: the universal configuration is obtained by adjoining arbitrary extra
tapes and heads to the prescribed simulation configuration, whose table position is at
most the serialization length of the decoded machine.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Checkpoint relation preserves halting]
\lean{Turing.universalRelation_halt}
\label{Turing.universalRelation_halt}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode, Turing.FinTM.rightCfg, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.universalRelation, Turing.universalSimulationCfg, Turing.universalTM}
\difficulty{1}
Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme, let $\alpha$ and $x$ be finite Boolean
words, let $s$ be a configuration of the machine decoded from $\alpha$ on input $x$, and
let $d$ be a configuration of the associated universal machine on
$\langle\alpha,x\rangle$. If $s$ and $d$ satisfy the checkpoint relation, then $s$ is
halted if and only if $d$ is halted.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Output preservation for related configurations]
\lean{Turing.universalRelation_output}
\label{Turing.universalRelation_output}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.EffectiveMachineCode, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.universalRelation, Turing.universalTM}
\difficulty{1}
Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme, and let $\alpha$ and $x$ be finite bit
strings. Let $\mathrm{src}$ be a configuration of the machine decoded from $\alpha$ on
input $x$, and let $\mathrm{dst}$ be a configuration of the universal machine associated
with $c$ on the paired input encoding of $\alpha$ and $x$. If there are a natural number
$p$ no greater than the length of the decoded machine's serialization, together with
tape contents and head positions for the canonizer's work tapes, such that
$\mathrm{dst}$ is the corresponding extended simulation configuration built from
$\mathrm{src}$ and $p$, then the two configurations have the same output word.
\end{lemma}
